name: MEAD, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Department's rules are consistent with the PFML Act, reasonably implement the program, and do not constitute an unconstitutional taking of private property.

name: HORTON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Engroff's speedy trial rights were not violated and the admission of the victim's video interview did not violate his confrontation or due process rights, as the statute was clarified to apply and cross-examination was available.

name: STANFILL, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that McLain did not clearly waive his privilege against self-incrimination and officers failed to clarify his ambiguous invocation of rights, thus his custodial statements must be suppressed.

name: CONNORS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that once a statute of limitations has expired, a claim cannot be retroactively revived as it impairs vested rights, making 14 M.R.S. § 752-C(3) unconstitutional.

name: DOUGLAS, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Maine Constitution does not prohibit the Legislature from retroactively repealing a statute of limitations, as a statute of limitations defense is not a vested right.

name: MEAD, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the right to hunt for food created by the amendment does not extend to illegal hunting, and therefore the Sunday hunting ban does not conflict with the Maine Constitution.

name: CONNORS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the PCR court misconstrued aspects of the relevant law regarding speedy trial protection and its interplay with ineffective assistance of counsel, requiring a remand for reconsideration.

name: CONNORS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that multiple prosecutorial errors, including improper "accountability" comments and references to the defendant's silence, combined with the context of potential racial bias, impaired the defendant's substantial rights and warranted a new trial to preserve the integrity of the judicial process.

name: STANFILL, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that section 6 of the Initiative is unconstitutional if NECEC acquired vested rights to proceed with Project construction, and remanded for factual determinations.

name: CONNORS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court did not err in denying the motion to dismiss under the Interstate Compact on Detainers, did not violate public trial rights with hallway bench conferences, and did not err in denying the mid-trial request for self-representation.

name: MEAD, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the emergency minimum wage provision was validly enacted under the Maine Constitution and Portland City Code, and that its effective date is January 1, 2022, based on the plain language of the ordinance.
